_note: Newest first. The top version must match MARKETING_VERSION in project.yml (tools/check_content.py checks). 1.0.0 is the App Store release.

releases.title: Signs and smiles
notes: Roads out of a map have a wooden signpost again. Walk up to it (a ? shows when you're close) and tap it to read where the road goes; tapping from afar walks you over first.
The title screen shows your hero facing you and breathing like they do in the game, with your companion close beside them doing its own idle bounce or sway.
The loading bar matches its percentage, and it learns how long each part of a map takes on your phone, so it fills at the real pace from the second visit on.
Hits in battle burst into a small fireball (hot core, flames, embers and a puff of smoke) instead of a cartoon star; critical hits blaze bigger, splash hits smaller, and heals glow green.

releases.title: Watch it fill
notes: Loading screens show a blue bar with a percentage instead of a spinner. The map is built a piece at a time behind it, so the bar moves as the ground, scenery, buildings and people go up.
In battle, names are smaller and sit right on top of each fighter's HP bar, so the field isn't covered in big labels.
Tap a quest in the Quests list to see its reward: gold, EXP, items with their icons, new looks and roads it opens. Tap a completed quest to see what it said and what you earned.
The title screen shows your active companion walking beside your hero.

releases.title: Tidy buttons
notes: Battle buttons sit in neat rows beside the big button instead of a tall column over your party, with More on top of the big button.
Pinned skills are round like the other battle buttons, with their MP cost underneath.

Rearranging works like the iPhone home screen: hold any battle button and they all wiggle. Drag one over another to take its place, onto the big button to make it the big one, or into the "Behind More" tray. Tap Done when you're happy.

releases.title: Back on the road
notes: Fixed: the game could crash while loading a map. Drawing the minimap's colours took so long on big maps that iOS stopped the app.
Deleting a game moved off the title screen, where its little × looked like it only closed the notice. It's now under Settings → Danger zone inside the game, and asks before deleting.

releases.title: Quieter streets
notes: Names step aside: your hero's and companions' names hide while you walk and come back when you stop.
Everyone else's name shows only when you walk up to them or tap them.
Arrange your battle buttons: hold any of them, then drag them into the order you like. The top one becomes the big button, so Attack can make way for a skill, and anything can go behind More.

releases.title: Glory in numbers
notes: Bigger battles: monster groups grow as you travel, from one to three in the first fields to as many as ten in the far lands, lined up in two rows.

Upgraded skills feel it: from level 2 your hero gathers power first, at 3 and 4 the hit bursts with rings, light rays and falling sparkles, and a mastered skill (level 5) blazes in gold with its name across the screen.
Class skills are spread over the long climb: new ones open at levels 15 to 70 instead of all before 30.
Play several heroes: a new game gets its own save, and the title screen lets you swipe between your games (and delete old ones).
The title screen shows each hero as they look in the game: race, hairstyle, colours and armour.
The quest list shows who gave you each quest, with their face and where they live, so you know where to report back.
Your hero walks on the Character screen and the title screen, turning to show every side.

releases.title: Within reach
notes: Battle buttons sit in one column right beside Attack: More at the bottom, Skills above it, and Capture, Items and your pinned skills stacking on top.
Your hero's name and gender are set for good when you create them; Customize still changes hairstyle and colours.
The minimap takes its colours from the map itself, so a purple wood or a snowy field looks the part.
Fixed light corners around the edge of the screen on moody maps like Twilight Woods.

releases.title: Into the mist
notes: Fixed a crash when continuing a game saved before 0.2.0 with friends in it.
The land beyond each map's edge now fades into a soft mist (a deep gloom in caves) instead of black.
A companion that faints stays down after the battle: it sits out fights and stops following you until a potion or a healer wakes it up, and earns no EXP from that fight.
Fixed the intro's first page running off the screen.

releases.title: A bigger Fairyland
notes: The world grows to 30 maps, with a world atlas, winding roads, caves, snowfall, icy ponds and busier towns.
Levels now run to 105 and beyond, and you join a guild at level 10.
Three new bosses: Grumpy Old Oak, Great Wisp and the Moon Rabbit Queen. Bosses can be fought again, and six of them may drop a rare colour of their armour.
Choose male, female or other and a hairstyle. Helmets and hoods now cover your hair, and stronger armour shows finer detail.
Every item and skill has its own art, magic weapons glow, and blacksmiths forge gear from monster materials.
Battles show names above each fighter with level and HP below; the map shows faces for you, your companion and your party.
A storybook soundtrack, new sound effects with volume settings, an intro for new heroes and a What's new list.
Friends you've made turn up around the world now and then, and can only join your party when they're nearby.

releases.title: First steps into Fairyland
notes: 14 maps joined by winding roads: Meadowbrook, Rainbow City and Goldburg, plus wild zones from Sunny Meadow to Moonglow.
Random encounters and turn-based battles fought where you stand. Big spells splash onto nearby monsters.
81 monsters across seven elements, with rare colour variants and three bosses.
Capture with Seal Stones and keep up to 5 companions. Your first hatches from the starter egg.
Start as a Novice and join a guild at level 5. Spend skill points to learn and power up skills.
Villagers and adventurers wander and chat. Befriend adventurers and bring two along in your party.
Customise hair, outfit and skin. Armour recolours your outfit and your weapon shows in hand.
Quests, shops, healers, checkpoints, an in-game calendar and a chiptune soundtrack.
